submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad content-word head: ordinary multi-word text with a content noun or other lexical word reads active-weak or stronger, because the head self-attends (weight near 1.0) on such tokens and emits a large deviant write, strongest (2.5-4.3) on nouns like studies, findings, results or recordings; on verbs, determiners and other words it instead attends back to an earlier token and writes near its mean. Only content-free prompts stay inactive regardless of length: repetitions of a single word or bare one-word utterances (peaks 0.0-0.6, well below the 1.09 line), while even short phrases with a content word (The cat sat, Dogs bark, Hi there) cross it.

rival_explanations: Any open-class word drives strong activity whenever it self-attends, so back-attending verbs like make, took or shown are just as strong as the nouns.
Only plural research-report nouns (studies, findings, results, discoveries) drive strong activity; singular nouns and concrete nouns like mat, dog or locals are weak.
